solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rubbish race for the more slap-headed?

parts.note: slap-headed is slang for bald, so more of it is the comparative
a dash is a short sprint

explanation.surface: A joke about a running event reserved for men with the shiniest scalps.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a race named after its entrants, with the descriptor coming first in the answer. Slap-head is British slang for a bald man.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is nonsense talk, the same thing rubbish means when used as an exclamation or noun for drivel.

clue.text: Republican cutting vegetable cap in France?

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another sits inside it

parts.note: beet is a root vegetable
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician slashing vegetable prices, with a cap on them in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the definition is a stereotype: the beret is the cap associated with France.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft round flat hat, the headwear popularly linked with Frenchmen.

clue.text: Cavalryman cordoning off a street in a UK city

indicators.note: a cordon surrounds an area, so the first piece goes round the following ones

parts.note: a lancer is a cavalry soldier with a lance
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier sealing off a road in a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: A UK city could be anything; the cavalryman's weapon is the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a historic city in Lancashire, north-west England.

clue.text: Exotic Al might undress? Hot stuff!

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take on an unusual new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Al might strip off, which an onlooker finds very sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' reads as an attractive person, but it means a fiery condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: English mustard is a particularly pungent yellow condiment, so it is literally hot in the spicy sense.

clue.text: Precious Liberal getting under Reckless's skin?

indicators.note: getting under someone's skin puts a thing inside them
the skin is the outer layer, so the word that owns it wraps round the inserted letter

parts.note: daring means reckless or bold
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A valuable Liberal politician irritating a rival called Reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Reckless was a British MP, so the capital looks like a name. Precious is the term of endearment, as Gollum's 'my precious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling and precious are both affectionate names for a beloved person.

clue.text: Wrongdoer nicks piano for a revolutionary ball

indicators.note: to nick is to steal and hold on to, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a sinner does wrong
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A thief steals a piano to sell for a lavish dance staged by rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: A revolutionary ball is a cricket delivery that turns sharply after bouncing because of the spin put on it.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a spinner is a ball bowled with heavy rotation, so it revolves through the air.

clue.text: Work, drink, love — then it's all over!

indicators.note: something turned all over is flipped round, so the letters before it are read from the end back

parts.note: to sup is to drink
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A weary summary of a life: toil, booze, romance, and then the end.
explanation.walkthrough: SUP followed by O gives SUPO, which read backwards is OPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition or artistic piece, a creative work in the noun sense.

clue.text: The papers state two at the top must leave

indicators.text: two at the top must leave
indicators.note: the first two letters depart, leaving the remainder

parts.note: to express is to state

explanation.surface: Newspapers report that a pair of senior figures has to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop EX from the start of EXPRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective name for newspapers and journalists.

clue.text: Saw a chap being reported as suited vigilante

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: to see is to spy, and a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man was reportedly spotted acting as a costumed vigilante.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel superhero who fights crime in a full-body suit, an unofficial vigilante.

clue.text: This sailor is a reason I'm randy at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor explains that being away at sea is why he feels lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the sailor's surface but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary seaman is the lowest rank of sailor in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: A deal-breaker sore general stores rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the concealed run is read in the opposite direction
the words 'sore general' store, or keep, the needed letters within them

parts.note: the run sits inside soRE GENERal, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A wounded military man who keeps supplies has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'sore general' backwards gives LARENEGEROS, with the answer in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reneger goes back on a promise or agreement, so is someone who breaks a deal.

clue.text: Foreigner former PM initially dismissed

indicators.note: the opening letter of the name is sent away, leaving the rest

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister was the first to be sacked, as an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the D from DISRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: To a British solver an Israeli is a national of another country, so a foreigner in the loose crossword sense.

clue.text: It breaks with no triad custom

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart and its parts can be reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone breaks with the habit of grouping things in threes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks with' reads as departing from custom, but 'breaks' scrambles IT along with NO TRIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a long-established practice handed down, which is what a custom is.

clue.text: Sprogs that can be a problem

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a matter of concern or difficulty

explanation.walkthrough: Sprogs is British slang for children; the surface jokes that kids can be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for a person's offspring and also an everyday word for a point of difficulty.

clue.text: Couple that can be a problem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to join or hook together
second meaning: a snag or setback

explanation.walkthrough: Couple looks like a noun for two people, which the surface suggests can be trouble, but it is a verb: to attach, as a trailer to a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch is to fasten one thing to another, and a hitch is also a temporary difficulty.

clue.text: Breathe in easily and sleep for a while

indicators.note: something done easily is loose and relaxed, so the letters are free to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to breathe gently and take a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathe in easily' reads as relaxation advice, but 'in' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hibernate spend the winter in a dormant state, a long period of sleep.

clue.text: European Union to block one masculine element

indicators.note: a blockage sits in the middle of a passage, so this letter is lodged within the following pair

parts.note: a German is a European
Roman numeral for one
U is a standard abbreviation for union
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: The European Union acting to stop a single man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' reads as the EU, but it splits: European is GERMAN and Union is U, which goes between I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a chemical element, a grey metalloid used in semiconductors.

clue.text: Staff to turn on sign in Italian shortly

indicators.note: the joined pieces are placed inside the last

parts.note: IT is a short form of Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read backwards

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: Workers about to switch on a sign written in Italian, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for workers, but it is the verb to man. Gin and it is an old British bar order using Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: In a moment means very soon, which is what shortly means as an adverb.

clue.text: Islanders Dominica evacuated in high numbers

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another
high in the sense of intoxicated, so the word that follows is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an evacuated place has its insides emptied out, so only the first and last letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of the island's name

explanation.surface: People were evacuated from Dominica in very large numbers, perhaps ahead of a hurricane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High numbers' looks like a quantity, but 'high' is the drunken scramble applied to the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermudans are the inhabitants of Bermuda, an Atlantic island territory, so they are islanders.

clue.text: Football team behind City with northern back

parts.note: arse is British slang for the backside

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A football club trailing Manchester City, with a northern defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind City' and 'back' sound like league tables and defenders, but they are wordplay. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous English Premier League football club based in north London.

clue.text: Land ringing a city in north-west America

indicators.note: a ring encircles something, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: to settle on a place is to land there
taken as written

explanation.surface: A territory surrounding a north-western American city.
explanation.walkthrough: SETTLE goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State, in the Pacific north-west of the USA.

clue.text: Long period of time ending in frustration

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of frustration

explanation.surface: A lengthy spell that finishes in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the period, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to have an intense desire, which is to long for something; both verbs.

clue.text: Sort of Sunday dinner making a universal stir

indicators.note: turning the article 'a' into the film-rating letter for universal swaps one letter for another

parts.note: a roast is the traditional British Sunday lunch or dinner
U is the British film classification for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A Sunday roast that is cooked in a huge pot and stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in ROAST is changed to U, the film rating meaning universal.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone, as in rousting them out of bed; both verbs.

clue.text: In an excited state, having taken a stimulant

parts.note: being up is being lively and excited
per means a, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Someone is wired after taking a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one picture of a drug-taker, but the clue splits before 'stimulant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine, the opposite of a downer.

clue.text: Patsy's Catholic primate, lecherous sort

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies its own letter
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
an ape is a primate
a lustful man is called an old goat

explanation.surface: A man called Patsy has a lecherous Catholic archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic primate' suggests a senior archbishop, but primate is just APE. The 's of Patsy's gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a dupe blamed for others' wrongdoing, which is exactly a scapegoat.

clue.text: Royal supporting art gallery — King Edward, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece goes beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries
R is the abbreviation for royal

explanation.surface: A royal backing a gallery, with a king as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch, but it is a British potato variety; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal for a potato, and King Edward is a popular British variety of potato.

clue.text: Drug aiming at quelling the first sign of gout

indicators.note: to quell is to suppress, so that letter is put down and removed

parts.note: aspiring means aiming high

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of gout

explanation.surface: A medicine intended to suppress the first symptoms of gout.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the G from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling and anti-inflammatory medication, so it is a drug.

clue.text: European politician in examination storm

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed inside the third

parts.note: a test is an examination
E is the abbreviation for European
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician under scrutiny causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Pull in topless bar surrounded by topless men

indicators.note: having lost its top means the first letter is taken off
one piece is enclosed within the other

parts.note: the word men with its first letter removed
the word bar with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: A topless bar where the clientele are bare-chested men too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' is used twice, once on each word, and the surface pretends it describes a strip club.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull in money is informal for to earn it, as in pulling in a good salary.

clue.text: Change new schedule that's upset Dynamo?

parts.note: to alter is to change
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: something upset is overturned, so in a down or across word the letters are flipped round

parts.note: a rota is a duty schedule

explanation.surface: A football fan wants a new fixture list after Dynamo were beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynamo looks like a team such as Dynamo Kyiv, but here it is the generator; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternator is an electrical generator, and a dynamo is another kind, so this is a definition by close example.
